description:
Check whether a crypto payment really settled and how much was ACTUALLY delivered, which is often not the amount the transaction claims. Use this before crediting anyone for an incoming payment.

Returns `delivered` (what truly moved), `claimed` (what the transaction says), `mismatch` (true when they disagree), and `warnings` naming the specific trap with a remedy. `ok` is true ONLY when the payment is final and meets everything you asserted in `expect`; anything uncertain returns ok:false, so it is safe to gate a credit on `ok`.

Chains: xrp, hedera, algorand, solana, ethereum, base, arbitrum, optimism, polygon, bnb, avalanche, linea, scroll, zksync, blast, mantle, celo, gnosis, bitcoin, litecoin.
Pass `expect` whenever you can. Without it this reports what happened; with it, it tells you whether to pay.
Read only: this never moves funds and never holds keys.

chain.description: Chain id. One of: xrp, hedera, algorand, solana, ethereum, base, arbitrum, optimism, polygon, bnb, avalanche, linea, scroll, zksync, blast, mantle, celo, gnosis, bitcoin, litecoin. Common aliases work too (eth, btc, matic, bsc, avax, sol, xrpl). Not needed for sandbox: references.

expect.description: What you believe should be true. Supplying this is what lets `ok` mean anything.

amount.description: Minimum acceptable amount in the asset's SMALLEST units, as a string (1 USDC = "1000000"). Compared against DELIVERED, never against the claimed amount.

asset.description: Expected asset symbol, e.g. USDC. Symbols are not unique, so prefer assetId.

assetId.description: Expected contract address or canonical token id. The reliable way to avoid being paid in a counterfeit token with the right symbol.

memo.description: Expected destination tag or memo, used to attribute a payment on a shared receiving address.

minConfirmations.description: Override the chain default before treating the payment as final.

to.description: The address that should have received it. Required on Bitcoin and Litecoin to get a meaningful delivered amount, because a UTXO transaction has many outputs and most of them may be change.

ref.description: The transaction hash or id. EVM: 0x + 64 hex. XRP: 64 hex. Solana: base58 signature. Bitcoin: 64 hex. Hedera: 0.0.1234-1700000000-123456789. Algorand: 52 base32 chars. Or a sandbox case like sandbox:xrp_partial_payment.

rpcUrl.description: Optional. Your own HTTPS RPC endpoint for this chain. Bypasses our rate limits entirely and usually returns faster.

name: verify_payment
